doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Dealing with feeling down and unreimbursed airline tickets
summary: She copes by talking to family and musicians, grieving the year's lost work, and describes hours on the phone with United over unrefunded tickets she books herself.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Do you have anything you do when you start to get down?

That’s a very good question. I talk to musicians, I talk to friends, I talk to my parents, I talk to my sister, I talk to my husband a lot you know. I talk it through you know, and I try to figure out what is — I actually feel that I have to grieve the loss of the year’s work. Basically it’s going to be — what it comes down to is the rest of the year’s work. It was so much work to put it together — plane tickets — the first few weeks of the quarantine were me on the phone to United trying to recoup what I could, because I paid out a lot in air tickets and they weren’t reimbursing them. And I’m saying but the flights are cancelled, can’t you just reimburse me the ticket? That was difficult. And so it was a combination of trying to figure out the unemployment, trying to see if there’s any grants, or trying to figure all these things out. And it was just all at once. And it just, it left me depressed because I didn’t get anywhere basically. I just got nowhere. And it was wasted hours it felt like, hours and hours on the phone and it was — yeah that got me down. That really got me down. And it got most musicians down because if you looked on FaceBook, if you talked to people, it was the same story. What are we going to do? This is bad.
It may have been mistaken assuming that the people booking you would provide you with that airfare, pay for those tickets themselves.

Yes. I’ve been booking them because you know I’m trying to get — I have a pretty good standing with United so I was trying to get United or United-affiliated flights. I always get compensated when I do the gig. So when the tour happens here’s your money and here’s your flight money you know. But you have to kind of book — you have to buy the © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

trip. And most people now, in the old days people always bought your flights. But in the last couple of years people are saying, “Try to get a flight around X amount.” Or people know me, they know I’m not going to be booking a business class flight or a seat. People know that I’m trying to get something on United or something else that is comparable on fare, and in summertime you’ve kind of got to get them a little earlier because summertime flights, especially to Europe, used to be very expensive. So sometimes, well it’s a negotiation, well that’s too high, see if you can go on a budget airline this time you know. It’s a lot of thought process that goes into getting the right flight you know. You can’t always get a direct. So that’s the thing, once you do the tour you are reimbursed. So that was a little bit of insult to injury because it was like the airlines, you’re getting some money from the federal government, can’t you just reimburse yourself? It doesn’t always work the way you want it to. That’s the lesson of all this.
